tob-10481: Israel Abrahams wanders the side roads of Jewish literature in this charming collection of essays. He introduces medieval Hebrew poets, old prayer books, and forgotten storytellers, showing how Jews wrote and read across a thousand years of exile. The book is a guided stroll for anyone curious about the quieter corners of Jewish letters.
tob-4081: Al-Farabi — the ‘Second Master’ after Aristotle — wrote the Book of Letters on speech, logic, and God-lore. The great 900s Muslim thinker wed Greek thought to Islamic teaching. This work shows his way at its freshest. It is needful for students of medieval thought.
tob-4181: The Warner brothers’ Shahnama gives book one of Firdausi’s great Persian king-epic — Iran’s kings and champions from fable’s dawn to story. Their verse-Englishing bore the King-Book to our readers. Rustam’s and his peers’ tales are world classics. The high grandeur unfolds volume by volume.
tob-10781: Turner’s Arbatel — Of the Magic of the Ancients — is the 1655 English of the gentle 1575 grimoire. It teaches the magic of the Olympic spirits through prayer and purity of life. Its humane wisdom influenced later Rosicrucian thought. The work remains uniquely beloved among grimoires.
cia-0000105881: An August 1964 report on the loss of an Indonesian Air Force transport aircraft over Malaysia. Indonesia and Malaysia were locked in the Confrontation, an undeclared war over the new Malaysian federation. The loss of a military plane in that theater would have raised the temperature between the two neighbors, and the CIA was watching closely.
cia-0000107981: A January 1977 weekly survey article on Pakistan's prediction that it could operate the Karachi nuclear plant. Pakistan's civilian nuclear program was widely suspected of hiding a weapons effort. The report captures analysts weighing official claims against the quiet evidence of a bomb in the making.
cia-0000108081: A February 1969 report on the capture of two American pilots during a three-day air attack in the Dan Neua area of Laos. The secret war in Laos was at full intensity, and airmen who went down faced capture by communist forces. The entry preserves one incident from a war that stayed officially unacknowledged for years.
cia-0000108481: The weekly terrorism situation report for April 29, 1981. Spring of that year brought its own catalog of incidents across Europe, the Middle East, and Latin America. The entry is one more weekly installment in the intelligence community's long effort to see patterns in political violence.
cia-0000118681: A January 1964 study of probable North Vietnamese reactions to various American courses of action. Before escalating, Washington wanted to know: what will Hanoi do if we do this? The document is war-gaming on paper — analysts playing the enemy's mind to guide the president's hand.
cia-0000119581: A November 1964 special report on Czechoslovakia trying a new role in the Soviet bloc. Prague was pushing for more independence within the communist alliance — more trade, more voice, less dictation from Moscow. The report spots the early stirrings of the reform movement that would become the Prague Spring.
cia-0000126881: A September 1968 report on Soviet treatment of Czechoslovak leaders dragged to Moscow. Dubcek and his colleagues were browbeaten into signing away their reforms. The document describes power at its rawest: the empire summoning its vassals to kneel.
cia-0000132481: Item 6 in the April 1960 series: the Venezuelan-Cuban rift possibly widening. Caracas was moving toward a break with Havana — democracy versus revolution. The document tracks the split: the neighbors, parting ways.
cia-0000132581: Item 12 in the September 1960 series: Brazil's president-elect possibly attempting mediation — the truncated title cuts off between whom. Brasilia fancied itself a peacemaker. The document is the mediation, mooted: the giant, offering its good offices.
cia-0000135881: A 1954 router with an attached memo titled with deleted words plus Calibaris briefing notes — the archive's quotes are garbled. The bureaucracy, routing. The entry is the slip: the memo, forwarded — the briefing, noted.
cia-0000136081: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN on closing down SARANAC. A station or operation, shuttered. The document is the closure: the site, shut.
cia-0000136381: A 1952 cable requesting that Castillo be contacted — the archive's spelling says requsting. The future invader, two years early. The document is the first touch: the colonel, contacted.
cia-0000136981: A 1954 cable to LINCOLN providing a status report for spares and supplies. The logistics, inventoried. The document is the status: the spares, counted.
un-ga-res-a-69-81: General Assembly Resolution A/69/81, adopted in 2014. The session's later business. The entry is the record: the eighty-first, dated.
un-ga-res-181: General Assembly Resolution 181, adopted in November 1947 — the Partition Plan for Palestine, dividing the British Mandate into Jewish and Arab states with an international Jerusalem. The vote passed 33 to 13 and lit the fuse of the Arab-Israeli conflict. The resolution is the division: the land, partitioned — the war, foreshadowed.
un-sc-res-81: Security Council Resolution 81, adopted in 1950. The wartime Council deliberated. The designation and year survive; the act lives in the text.
un-sc-res-681: Security Council Resolution 681, cataloged with the year 1949 — the numbering belongs to 1990, a deep mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is doubted.
un-sc-res-1381: Security Council Resolution 1381, adopted in 2001 — aligned. The Council's business continued. The number and year endure; the decision is in the text.
un-sc-res-1481: Security Council Resolution 1481, adopted in 2003 — aligned. The Council deciding. The number and year survive; the decision lives in the text.
un-sc-res-1681: Security Council Resolution 1681, cataloged with the year 2000 — the numbering suggests 2006, a mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is doubted.
un-sc-res-1881: Security Council Resolution 1881, cataloged with the year 2008 — the numbering suggests 2009, a small inconsistency. The designation is kept; the date is questioned.
cia-0000132681: A 1961 CIA Cuba file — number 0000132681. The paper trail lengthened. The document is the trail: the files, accumulating.
cia-0000132781: A 1960 CIA file on Cuban developments, numbered 0000132781. The year's last folders. The document is the last: the year, filed away.
cia-0000135681: A 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents, numbered 0000135681. The fateful year's papers. The entry is the fate: the year, 1961.
cia-0000139481: A 1988 CIA file on Project Sun Streak, numbered 0000139481. The remote viewers' paperwork. The document is the paperwork: the psychics, filed.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d81: Prime Minister Churchill to President Roosevelt, October 31, 1943 — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 81. A second letter that day. The message is the doubling: the day, busy.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d181: The Most Secret Protocol of the Moscow Conference — the truncated title cuts off the date — Document 181. More secret than secret. The protocol is the most-secret: the deals, deepest.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d281: A memorandum by the British Chiefs of Staff, November 22, 1943 — Document 281, closing the batch. The British planners' paper. The memo is the close: the batch, complete.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d381: A report from the Office of Strategic Services — the truncated title cuts off the date — Document 381. The OSS weighed in. The report is the spies': the OSS, assessing.
arxiv-2605-08881: When a user buys after seeing five ads, which ad deserves the credit? Yuguang Liu, Luyao Xia, Hu Liu, Zhangxi Yan, Jian Liang, and colleagues tackle multi-touch attribution with front-door causal methods, assigning credit across the creator ecosystem more honestly. The 2026 paper brings causal inference to advertising measurement.
arxiv-2605-09181: Tracking eyes through retinal images could diagnose disease — if the tracking survives real-world noise. Bo Wen, Dillon Lohr, Yatong An, and colleagues establish robust retinal eye tracking with a weakly supervised framework that needs little labeled data. The 2026 paper is medical computer vision built for the clinic.
arxiv-2605-09281: Mixture-of-experts models are huge, and quantizing their experts without wrecking them is delicate. Hongyaoxing Gu, Xinzhe Chen, Lijuan Hu, and Fangfang Liu propose TileQ: efficient low-rank quantization with 2D tiling. The 2026 paper shrinks giant mixture-of-experts models carefully.
arxiv-2605-09481: Time-sensitive networking — Ethernet with hard deadlines for factories and cars — is a specialized world. Rubi Debnath, Daniel Bujosa Mateu, Luxi Zhao, and colleagues benchmark how well LLMs handle it with TSNBench. The 2026 paper tests whether chatbots can do industrial networking.
arxiv-2605-09581: Event cameras see only changes — perfect for fast motion — and contrast maximization sharpens their noisy output. Michał Filipkowski, Marcin Kowalczyk, and Tomasz Kryjak build a dedicated FPGA hardware architecture for it. The 2026 paper is neuromorphic vision fully realized in silicon.
arxiv-2605-09681: Video diffusion models autoregress frame by frame, and the KV cache grows monstrous across long generations. Yicheng Ji, Zhizhou Zhong, Jun Zhang, and colleagues compress it hybrid-style with Forcing-KV. The 2026 paper makes autoregressive video generation leaner and faster.
arxiv-2605-09881: Jet-taggers classify particle jets at the LHC with neural networks; mechanistic interpretability dissects how they decide. This 2026 paper opens the black box of jet classification. It is particle physics meets interpretability at the high-energy frontier of modern physics today.
arxiv-2605-09981: Yeti tokenizes protein structures compactly — for reconstruction and multi-modal generation alike. Nabin Giri, Steven Farrell, Kristofer E. Bouchard, and colleagues build the compact tokenizer. The 2026 paper is protein AI with a compact vocabulary. It compresses the language of proteins.
arxiv-2605-10081: Microwave imaging in complex multipath environments needs polarization-aware ray-tracing enhanced back-projection. Han Na, Quanfeng Wang, and colleagues develop the algorithm. The 2026 paper is microwave imaging through clutter. It sees clearly through multipath interference, fully polarization-aware.
plos-pone-0003381: Eye researchers traced a surprising villain in blindness in this 2008 immunology paper. Interleukin-10, usually a calming immune signal, was found to promote abnormal blood-vessel growth in the oxygen-starved eye, a condition called neovascularization and the leading cause of blindness. By steering how macrophages react to low oxygen, IL-10 drives the very vessel overgrowth that threatens vision.
plos-pone-0003481: HIV researchers found immune cells defending themselves in this 2008 paper. Individual CD4 T cells, the virus's favorite target, can produce their own antiviral CCR5-blocking chemicals, shielding themselves from R5 strains of HIV-1. That self-protection suggests some cells resist infection from within, a natural defense worth understanding for future therapies.
plos-pone-0003581: Cancer geneticists linked a kidney gene to cysts and tumors in this 2008 mouse study. Deleting FLCN, the gene behind Birt-Hogg-Dubé syndrome, produced polycystic kidneys and renal neoplasia, confirming it as a tumor suppressor. The mouse model gives researchers a living system for a rare inherited cancer syndrome.
plos-pone-0003681: In 2008, Renesto, Rovery, and Schrenzel eavesdropped on a germ at the bite site. Rickettsia conorii, the tick-borne cause of Mediterranean spotted fever, was caught switching its genes on inside the skin sore. The transcriptional snapshot shows what the bacterium does first, at the very spot where infection begins.
plos-pone-0003781: Martinovic, Gruber, and Müller asked how the brain binds features into objects in this 2008 paper. Recording brain activity, they studied how visual features and their combinations are coded in neural assemblies. The work probes the first steps of turning scattered features into recognized things.
plos-pone-0003881: In 2008, a team argued fishing starves whole ecosystems, not just target fish. Catches export mass and energy that higher food-web levels would have used, depleting the system's secondary production. The paper reframes overfishing as ecosystem overeating, with the sea's food web paying the bill.
plos-pone-0003981: In 2008, Byakika-Tusiime, Chinn, and Oyugi tested generic HIV drugs against brand names. The steady-state bioequivalence trial compared generic and brand formulations of stavudine, lamivudine, and nevirapine. Generics matched the innovator drugs in the blood levels patients actually get. The result backs affordable generics as the mainstay of HIV treatment worldwide.
plos-pone-0004081: In 2009, Merad, Porumb, and Zargarian found a hidden grip in HIV's toolkit. An unusual helix-turn-helix motif in HIV-1 integrase bound viral DNA. The same motif also grabbed the host factor LEDGF. The double grip marks a target for blocking integration.
plos-pone-0004181: In 2009, Yang, Zhang, and Xu found a blood signal for a deadly fever. Serum platelet-activating factor acetylhydrolase activity marked severe leptospirosis cases. The enzyme's level tracked deadly lung bleeding risk. The handy marker could flag patients needing urgent care sooner.
plos-pone-0004281: In 2009, Parker, Barkley, and Rino unmasked a TB wall-builder. The Rv3802c protein acted as a phospholipase/thioesterase in TB bacteria. An antimycobacterial compound blocked it. The enzyme's role spotlights a new drug target. The wall-building enzyme is key to TB's armor.
plos-pone-0345881: Why do gig workers keep driving, delivering, and freelancing when the pay is uncertain? This paper builds a typology — a map of types — of what motivates them, from the love of flexible hours to the need for cash. Sorting intrinsic and extrinsic drives, it gives platforms and policymakers a clearer picture of what actually keeps gig workers going.
plos-pone-0358781: Preeclampsia — dangerous high blood pressure in pregnancy — kills mothers in Kenya every year, and vitamin D deficiency is widespread. This matched case-control study compared vitamin D levels in Kenyan mothers who developed preeclampsia with those who did not. The results test whether a cheap supplement could become part of prevention.
plos-pone-0351281: Searching encrypted documents without decrypting them is a hard problem — harder still in Arabic, with its rich morphology. This paper evaluates preprocessing methods for dynamic searchable symmetric encryption of Arabic text. The empirical framework tells developers which text processing choices make encrypted Arabic search both fast and accurate.
plos-pone-0355381: A wild plant may protect the stomach from alcohol’s assault. This in vivo study showed Tragopogon coelesyriacus attenuates ethanol-induced gastric ulcers by calming oxidative stress, inflammation, and cell death. The plant emerges as a serious candidate for future ulcer-fighting drugs rooted in traditional knowledge.
plos-pone-0353681: Virus surveillance data has gaps — but epidemics don’t wait for complete records. This paper developed methods for estimating cumulative incidence from partially missing time series of respiratory viral infections. The math fills the gaps honestly, with uncertainty shown rather than hidden.
plos-pone-0358481: Stress ties the gut in knots — in pigs as in people. This paper tested surface electromyography as a non-invasive method for detecting stress-induced changes in gastrointestinal motility in pigs. The skin-surface readings offer researchers a painless, continuous window into the stressed gut.
plos-pone-0357381: Could electrical stimulation of muscles lift a depressed mind? This pilot randomized controlled trial protocol will test functional electrical stimulation for major depressive disorder. The planned trial explores an unconventional idea: whether zapping muscles can meaningfully improve mood.
plos-pone-0357181: In the ICU, immune status quietly shaped who survived the pandemic — and the gap widened late. This study found that outcomes of immunocompromised and non-immunocompromised patients diverged late in the pandemic. The late split reveals how the virus’s evolution changed the odds for the most vulnerable.
plos-pone-0356181: Exercise builds muscle — but the right recipe differs for rheumatic disease and age-related muscle loss. The Care for Muscle (C4M) study protocol will test the effects of exercise on muscle strength and characteristics in these groups. The planned trial tailors training to fragile muscles that can’t take standard programs.
plos-pone-0357581: Liquid bio-slurry can replace chemical nitrogen fertilizer for hot pepper farming. This Ethiopian study optimized nitrogen delivery via bio-slurry equivalent rations for hot pepper and soil productivity in the Amhara region. The organic approach boosts yields sustainably while cutting dependence on synthetic fertilizer.
plos-pone-0357281: Removing the superior cervical ganglion — a sympathetic nerve hub — worsened aortic dissection in mice. The finding implicates sympathetic nerves directly in aortic disease progression. The mouse model reveals a previously underappreciated mechanism that could reshape how scientists think about aortic catastrophe.
plos-pone-0355981: Microglia — the brain’s immune cells — respond to demyelination in complex, shifting ways. This paper mapped their multifaceted response in the cuprizone model of demyelination. The detailed portrait reveals microglia as dynamic players in myelin damage and repair, not mere bystanders.
plos-pone-0356781: A common lab protein — bovine serum albumin — can prime the mouse brain for a stronger reaction to bacterial toxins. This paper showed BSA sensitizes the mouse brain to lipopolysaccharides. The finding is a cautionary tale for neuroscientists: even ‘inert’ lab reagents can skew results.
plos-pone-0356381: Primary ocular-adnexal non-Hodgkin lymphoma — cancer around the eye — is rare and poorly documented in Latin America. This Peruvian cohort study reported an 18-year experience with the disease. The long-term data give regional oncologists the evidence base they’ve been missing.
plos-pone-0356281: Why do Pakistani women use — or avoid — contraception? This paper revisited the classic health belief model, adding fertility preferences and health system interaction as keys to contraceptive use. The enriched model explains decisions that simpler frameworks miss, pointing family planning programs toward what actually matters.
plos-pone-0356881: Some elementary schoolers simply refuse to go — and resilience may be the difference. This paper examined the associations of solution-building skills and resilience with school refusal behavior among elementary students. The findings point schools toward building children’s coping capacity rather than merely punishing absence.
plos-pone-0356481: Immigrants’ health in England and Wales varies dramatically by country of birth — but detailed data were missing. This total-population, repeated cross-sectional study measured immigrant life expectancy and disability-free life expectancy by detailed birth country. The granular findings reveal which migrant groups thrive and which suffer — essential for equitable health policy.
plos-pone-0355481: When mothers work, do Nepali children eat better or worse? This paper examined the impact of maternal employment on child health and nutrition with evidence from Nepal. The findings untangle income gains from time losses — informing policies that support working mothers without shortchanging children.
plos-pone-0355781: Biochar enhanced with rock minerals holds a hydrogen puzzle. This paper investigated pyrogenic coatings, mineral redox chemistry, and pore accessibility in rock-enhanced biochar. Solving the puzzle unlocks biochar’s full potential for carbon sequestration and soil restoration.
plos-pone-0354981: Glioblastoma might be attacked with repurposed Alzheimer’s and ovarian cancer drugs — activated by ultrasound. This paper used positive-unlabeled learning plus 3D bioprinting to repurpose drugs as sonosensitizers for glioblastoma. The AI-guided repurposing could fast-track new weapons against the deadliest brain cancer.
plos-pone-0355681: Yeast cells tune gene expression to glucose availability through layered regulation. This paper uncovered dual regulatory mechanisms controlling YGP1 expression in Saccharomyces cerevisiae in response to glucose. The findings illuminate the sophisticated nutrient sensing of biology’s favorite model organism.
plos-pone-0355181: Sudden sensorineural hearing loss — waking up deaf in one ear — may involve homocysteine. This prospective clinical study found evidence for hyperhomocysteinemia in these patients. The findings suggest a blood marker — and possibly a treatable metabolic contributor — for a frightening condition.
europmc-pmc2850381: Before a cell divides, its nucleus and centrosome must move into position. This 2010 paper shows the motor proteins dynein and kinesin-1, linked by Bicaudal D2, associate with nuclear pores to regulate that positioning during mitotic entry. The authors map the machinery. Their work reveals the logistics behind cell division.
europmc-pmc2870981: A century-old chemical reaction keeps finding new tricks. This 2010 review tours new developments in the Friedel-Crafts alkylation, from green chemistry to asymmetric catalysis. The authors show an old workhorse renewed. Their tour connects classic organic chemistry to modern clean methods.
europmc-pmc2872881: Pea aphids live with many microbes yet rarely get sick, and this 2010 paper asks why. The authors survey immunity and other defenses in the pea aphid Acyrthosiphon pisum. Their overview reveals unusual immune gaps. The work explains how a major crop pest tolerates its germ load.
europmc-pmc2885081: Chitin and chitosan, from shells and fungi, need careful characterization before use. This 2010 review surveys spectroscopic methods for their structural analysis. The authors compare the tools of the trade, from infrared to NMR. Their guide helps labs verify exactly what material they have.
europmc-pmc2888581: Mothers and children die in huge numbers across Sub-Saharan Africa, and this 2010 paper asks where and why. The authors map the deaths and their causes. Their analysis points to preventable gaps in care. The paper became a blueprint for saving lives in the region.
europmc-pmc2896381: Seeing biology in 3D takes the right tools. This 2010 paper presents a high-level 3D visualization API for Java and ImageJ, the beloved microscope software. The authors' interface lets biologists render volumes with little code. Their tool brought 3D views to everyday lab microscopes everywhere.
europmc-pmc2908081: HPV's role in throat cancers needed quantifying, and this 2010 meta-analysis delivers. The authors weigh HPV's impact on cancer risk and survival in head and neck squamous cell carcinomas. Their pooling clarifies the virus's toll. The work refined prognosis and vaccine arguments.
europmc-pmc2939781: Bile duct cancers are rare and brutal, and this 2010 Japanese study compares treatments. The authors test gemcitabine alone versus paired with cisplatin in biliary tract cancer. Their multicenter data favors the combo. The result shaped care guidelines in Asia. Oncologists still follow its lead.
europmc-pmc3002981: Stressed cells reprogram their tRNA decorations. This 2010 paper shows cells retune tRNA chemical marks when stress hits. The authors uncover the retuning with systems math. Their work links tRNA to stress defense. The marks act like dimmer switches on genes.
europmc-pmc3061881: Wiping mouse gut germs reshapes the gut. This 2011 paper shows antibiotics that clear mouse gut germs remake the gut lining. The authors reveal the reshaping. Their work informs germ science. The lining thins without its germs. Repopulating germs reverses the damage.
europmc-pmc6536981: Pancreatic cancer that cannot be surgically removed leaves few options - but MRI-guided radiation can aim higher doses precisely at the tumor while sparing nearby organs. This study reports outcomes for inoperable patients treated with adaptive MR-guided radiotherapy, including dose-escalated cases. The results suggest sharper targeting may extend survival where surgery is impossible.
europmc-pmc6549181: One small SARS protein - ORF-8b - punches above its weight: it stresses infected cells and trips the NLRP3 inflammasome, a molecular fire alarm. Researchers showed this viral piece drives the runaway inflammation behind severe SARS. Pinpointing the culprit protein suggests ways to douse the immune overreaction in coronavirus infections.
europmc-pmc6600381: A severed spinal cord triggers a destructive chain reaction - the secondary injury - that kills more nerve cells than the initial blow. This review weighs mesenchymal stem cells as a treatment: what trials show so far, where the approach falls short, and what cell therapy's future may hold. Hope is real, but so are the hurdles.
europmc-pmc6642581: Severe flu kills not just through the virus but through the body's own firestorm. This review covers influenza's path to critical illness: how the virus injures airways and how immune overreaction finishes the job. Understanding both arms guides intensive-care treatment of flu's worst cases.
europmc-pmc6700281: Which protein-coding DNA changes raise diabetes risk? Scanning the exomes - the protein-coding 1% - of 20,791 people with type 2 diabetes against 24,440 controls, researchers hunted strong-effect variants across five ancestries. The haul points to genes whose malfunction drives the disease.
europmc-pmc6722781: Neutrophils - first-responder immune cells - can explode, casting webs of DNA studded with antimicrobials. These neutrophil extracellular traps snare pathogens but also drive disease, from cystic fibrosis to cancer. This review covers their formation, their harm, and drugs that tame them.
europmc-pmc6737581: Drug-resistant germs are outrunning old surveillance - but DNA sequencing can track them. This review shows how genomics follows antimicrobial resistance around the globe: reading pathogen genomes to spot resistance genes and their spread. The genomic watchtower guides containment before outbreaks ignite.
gao-gaoreports-b-310081: One of GAO's biggest consolidated bid-protest rulings of 2007, joining nine docket numbers filed by timber companies — Poston Logging, Shasta Green, Sierra Cedar, Trinity River, and others. The challengers contested Forest Service timber-sale decisions under shared legal questions. The decision walks through each protest, applies procurement and timber-sale law, and shows how GAO handles mass filings from a whole industry at once.
gao-gaoreports-b-299981: A 2007 GAO ruling on two linked contract fights from Navarro Research and Engineering, Inc. The tech firm said the agency's award was off; the ruling weighs each claim and calls it. For engineering shops in the federal market, the published call shows how GAO grades a bid when the work is brains, not bricks.
gao-gaoreports-b-309181: Spy-agency deal paperwork drew GAO's fiscal eye in 2007 — could the counterintelligence office legally use an interagency pact this way? The ruling reads the money statutes against the agreement line by line. Even the shadow world, GAO reminds, spends by the book and answers for its deals.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-781: Nobody was steering the flu ship in 2007 — GAO's report says federal outbreak leadership stayed fuzzy and the national plan stayed thin. The findings demand named leaders and a real playbook before the big one hits. Another warning the nation would wish it had heeded sooner.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-881: Fish rules needed better math in 2007 — GAO's report says the fisheries service owed sharper economic analysis for its proposed changes. The findings press for numbers that hold up before nets get restricted. Conservation, the report argues, is strongest when its economics are honest.
gao-gaoreports-b-299781: Healthcare Technology Solutions International took its July 2007 contract fight to GAO, and this ruling is the verdict. The firm said the agency's health-tech award was unfair; the call tests the claims. Medical IT deals get the same fair-bid scrutiny as any federal buy.
gao-gaoreports-b-299381: LexisNexis took its April 2007 contract fight to GAO, and this ruling is the verdict. The legal-research giant said the agency's award was unfair; the call tests the protest. Even the keepers of the law books must argue their case by the book.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-281: Spare parts were taking too long to buy in 2007, and GAO's report says the Pentagon could better manage its acquisition lead times. The findings target the delays. The report's logic: the war machine should not wait on its own supply chain.
openalex-w7206213381: Some texts repeat the same words over and over; others use varied vocabulary. This computational linguistics paper proposes a simple way to sort documents into high and low lexical repetition using Yule's K, a classic measure of vocabulary concentration, paired with k-means clustering. The authors test the method with Monte Carlo simulation. A neat, technical contribution to the toolkit for automatically characterizing writing style.
pmc-13466781: This 2026 oncology paper applies next-generation sequencing — reading the full DNA of tumors — to real-world colorectal cancer patients and links the molecular profiles to clinical outcomes. Rather than a controlled trial, it shows what gene-guided care looks like in everyday practice. The findings help oncologists match patients to targeted drugs.
pmc-13458981: In this 2026 virology study, doctors in Zambia detected enterovirus D68 in hospitalized children suffering severe respiratory infections. EV-D68 is best known from outbreaks in wealthy countries, so documenting it in southern Africa fills a surveillance gap. The paper adds evidence that this virus circulates more widely than global tracking suggests.
pmc-13428181: This 2026 consensus statement from Belgian experts lays out biomarker-based diagnosis and care pathways for Alzheimer's disease in the era of disease-modifying treatments — drugs that slow the disease rather than just easing symptoms. With treatments finally targeting the biology, diagnosis has to keep up. The statement gives clinicians a practical roadmap.
pmc-13437081: A 2026 (listed 2025) paper clarifying contradictions about transportability in 17OHP-C trials for preterm birth, using doubly debiased machine learning. Whether trial results apply elsewhere is a critical question. The advanced methods give a cleaner answer.
pmc-13563881: In this 2026 radiology paper, combining CT examination process optimization with a vial-sharing strategy for contrast agents proved economical and practical for hospitals. Contrast is expensive and wasted. The combined approach saves money without hurting care.
pmc-13487581: This 2026 autoethnography explored recovery as an intersubjective process — experiential knowledge in mental health through the author's own story. Recovery happens between people, not just within them. The personal account is the method and the message.
pmc-13470181: A 2026 review of extracellular vesicle-mediated immune crosstalk in rheumatoid arthritis synovium — mechanistic insights and translational challenges. Joint-lining vesicles orchestrate inflammation. The review maps the communication network.
pmc-13504281: This 2026 microbiology paper phenotypically and biochemically characterized PAC-1, a class C beta-lactamase. The resistance enzyme was profiled. The characterization informs drug design.
pmc-13501881: A 2026 physical chemistry paper on anion states and dissociation pathways of a universal radiosensitizer model compound. The electron attachment chemistry was mapped. The pathways inform radiotherapy.
pmc-13484881: This 2026 paper developed and internally validated perioperative prediction models for acute kidney injury after lung transplantation. The kidney risk was modeled. The models guide prevention.
pmc-13473181: A 2026 mouse study showing Lactiplantibacillus plantarum AS21 attenuated sex-biased glucose intolerance in aging mice via gut mucosal microbiota-derived citrulline. The probiotic's citrulline mediated the benefit. The sex-biased effect is the nuance.
pmc-13454781: This 2026 review covered three decades of soil nitrous oxide research — insights and gaps. The greenhouse gas's soil science was synthesized. The gaps chart the future.
pmc-13451081: A 2026 software paper introducing robustocs — robust optimal contribution selection. The breeding optimization tool is the deliverable. The robustness is the feature.
pmc-13481781: In this 2026 health policy paper, an unintended complementarity was found — China's outpatient pooling policy increased inpatient services. The policy backfired interestingly. The complementarity is the lesson.
pmc-13526881: A 2026 space physics paper: plasma wave observations from the Juno spacecraft at the Jovian bow shock. Jupiter's shock waves were recorded. The observations are the data.
pmc-13495581: A 2026 NLP paper introducing EmoTweetID — a dataset of Indonesian tweets for emotion classification and word embedding construction. The Indonesian emotion data were released. The dataset is the resource.
pmc-13474481: In this 2026 paper, an integrative neurocognitive model of metacognition and emotion regulation in ADHD was proposed — from brain circuits to self-regulation. The model unifies the circuits. The integration is the theoretical advance.
pmc-13435981: A 2026 umbrella review on inclusion of sex and gender in clinical practice guidelines. The guidelines' sex-gender gaps were synthesized. The review demands better inclusion.
pmc-13435581: In this 2026 paper, impaired NADH-linked mitochondrial respiration disrupted ventral midbrain neuronal programs in POLG disease. The mitochondrial defect broke the dopamine neurons' development. The disrupting is the disease mechanism.
pmc-13444181: This 2026 review covered sustained-release local anesthetics — advances in drug delivery systems for prolonged postoperative analgesia. The long-acting pain relief was surveyed. The review is the drug delivery outlook.
pmc-13420281: A 2026 case report of unusual sequential development of multiple sclerosis, thymoma, myasthenia, and lymphoma in the same patient. The autoimmune cascade was documented. The case is the medical rarity.
pmc-13449481: A 2026 paper developing and validating an integrated machine learning model for recurrence-free survival prediction in clear cell renal cell carcinoma. The AI forecasted the kidney cancer's return. The model is the prognostic tool.
pmc-13421281: A 2026 prospective study of the association between baseline ultra-processed food consumption and future adherence to 24-hour movement guidelines in children (the title is truncated). The junk food's activity legacy was tested. The association is the finding.
arxiv-2606-16081: A pure math paper about the playbook of shape-math: how big math frames act on spaces. It builds 'cut and paste' moves for neat gangs of math things (simple-minded systems) inside mirror-like frames. The fine print is for algebra pros only.
arxiv-2606-16181: Altermagnets are a fresh-found class of magnet stuff with odd traits that may drive next-gen gear. This paper eyes the gem-cut of Ca3(Ru,Ti)2O7, a hoped-for 'polar' case, to test if its build truly earns the name. It is rock-physics for magnet-tech hunters.
arxiv-2606-16281: Masked diffusion language models generate text by filling in blanks, and ensembling several of them can improve quality — but which model should lead at each step? This paper tracks reliable generation trajectories to decide who leads decoding when. It targets AI researchers improving diffusion-based alternatives to standard autoregressive models.
arxiv-2606-16781: Quantum chromodynamics (QCD) describes quarks and gluons — the building blocks of matter. This paper pushes 'QCD-like theories' to next-to-next-to-leading order precision with two non-degenerate fermion flavors. It is a precision theory paper for particle physicists. Sharper math, truer quarks.
arxiv-2606-16881: Robot teams mapping together must merge their maps — distributed SLAM. SGM-SLAM matches scene graphs (maps of objects and relations) to do it with less data. It is for robotics researchers building multi-robot mapping. Many bots, one map. Graphs beat raw points.
